As shown in #64868, a number of newer models don't come wiht a macAddr
attributes, so for those fall back to the wireless address.

This could be hidden by the python-songpal library but for now this will

Hey there @rytilahti, @shenxn, mind taking a look at this pull request as it has been labeled with an integration (`songpal`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L879) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Should we tag it for a patch release?

I _think_ it would be fine to be in a patch release. But I'm not entirely sure whether the fact that entities might go from "no unique id" to "have unique id" would complicate things.

(The unique ID is only changed for entities that currently wouldn't have one, because they don't have a wired address — that's why it prefers the wired mac as unique identifier.)

A possible complication would be if the user would roll back the update, the entity registry would still have the entry with the unique_id and not allow the entity without the unique_id to get its old entity_id but generate a new entity_id with a suffix.

Is non-backwards compatibility a blocker here, and if yes, what is be the proper way to solve this? My personal opinion is that this is ready to go as the pros clearly outweigh the cons. Also, I don't think most of the other integrations do offer a working downgrade path either..
We should definitely merge this. It's just a question of do we include it in a patch release?
Ah, sorry for being unclear. My previous comment was for getting this into the next patch release, but I'll ping on discord to get another opinion on that.

issue_context.title: Songpal not generating unique ID
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Have a Sony SRS-RA3000 and a Sony SRS-RA5000 in the same network both are detected but then looking at the created device and entries the two are inter connected and mixed up.

Other devices like HT-ZF9 and SRS-ZR5 works as they should.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.12.10

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

songpal

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/songpal/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.media_player] Platform songpal does not generate unique IDs. ID  already exists - ignoring media_player.srs_ra5000_sony
```


### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
Hey there @rytilahti, @shenxn, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`songpal`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L876) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

The unique id is based on the [mac address of the device](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/songpal/media_player.py#L213) which should be unique, so unfortunately I don't have a quick solution for this at this point :-(
Strange, they definitely have different MAC addresses...

@rytilahti I know what it can be :-) this devices do not have a eth only wifi so from songpal status the reported info is
`System information: Sysinfo(bdAddr='XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX', macAddr='', version='1.41', wirelessMacAddr='XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX', bssid=None, ssid='XXXXXX_5G', bleID='XXXXXXXX')`
and
`System information: Sysinfo(bdAddr='XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX', macAddr='', version='1.41', wirelessMacAddr='XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX', bssid=None, ssid='XXXXXX_5G', bleID='XXXXXXXX')`

so if this info and only the macAddr is used by HA that could explain why it has the same id.
@freke Ah, indeed.. There's #63145 that includes a change (fallback to wirelessMacAddr, ping @Flameeyes) related to this, perhaps it could be extracted into a separate PR :thinking:
I'll see if I can find some time for making that change earlier rather than with the rest of the changes I'm planning. Unfortunately dayjob has me knee deep for the next couple of weeks 😭

review_comments: I'm not sure why the test is failing, but I think the `unique_id` needs also be adjusted. If the default value for those renders to an empty string, having a combination of both addresses should not break anything, but alas I don't have a device to test it at the moment :-(

Yeah I saw how that failed. Turns out I was testing a single case instead of the whole unit, oops!

I changed the test to not use a mock at all for SysInfo. This makes it more reliable overall.
